title: Zero-Freeness of Independence Polynomials in Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
topic: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
description: We investigate the absence of real zeros in the independence polynomial of random d-regular graphs for degrees up to the replica symmetry breaking (RSB) th...
abstract: We investigate the absence of real zeros in the independence polynomial of random $d$-regular graphs for degrees up to the replica symmetry breaking (RSB) threshold. The study combines a deterministic graph-generation routine, a Durand--Kerner root-finding implementation, and a Python-based zero-detection routine. We prove that the algorithm preserves an acyclic directed-acyclic-graph invariant during the iterative refinement of candidate roots, guaranteeing that no spurious real roots are introduced. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V45 platform yields a mean latency of 33 504.14 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 29 847 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261030_230123_zero-freeness_for_random_regul}.
